name: Yamini
headline: Turn Marriott’s booking data into guests who keep coming back.
saw: Across a hotel group, the offer a guest sees on arrival, after a stay or in a booking email tends to be the same for a business traveller, a family and a long-stay guest alike.

Every stay already produces a signal: which rooms are booked, how far ahead, when a guest changes dates or cancels, and who books again. Today that signal sits in revenue reports, not in the message the guest receives.
Cross-sell, upsell and retention campaigns are usually built by hand, per segment, per month. The guest who is about to lapse this week gets the same offer as everyone else, or none at all.
help_intro: Three places where an AI that decides per guest, not per segment, pays for itself in the first quarter.

cases.head: Stop the lapsed guest before they leave
cases.text: Per guest signals from booking dates, cancellations and gaps between stays flag who is about to lapse. The right offer, channel and moment is picked for each guest.
cases.kpi_label: lower churn, measured at Flytxt telecom clients

cases.head: Offer the next stay that fits
cases.text: Next best room, brand or length of stay per guest, triggered by how they book. Fewer blanket promotions, more offers where they actually lift the stay.
cases.kpi_label: conversion vs untargeted campaigns, Tier-1 African MNO

cases.head: Keep guests booking between stays
cases.text: Personal nudges in email and SMS for each guest, from a new destination to a weekend idea, so every guest has a reason to book again before the next season.
cases.kpi_label: streaming activity at an OTT client
